issues.sym: The oil level drops noticeably between oil changes, the low oil light comes on, or the dipstick reads low with no leak under the car.
issues.why: Early versions of this engine had piston rings that let oil slip past and burn off. Subaru settled a class action and covered testing and engine repairs for a set period, which has now run out for most cars.
issues.next: Check the oil level at every other fill-up and top it off right away if it is low. Running this engine low on oil can destroy it, so have a shop run an oil consumption test if it keeps dropping.

issues.sym: A sudden ticking or rattling from the engine, rough running, a flashing check engine light, or the engine stalling and not restarting.
issues.why: A batch of valve springs was not strong enough and can crack over time. A broken spring lets the engine misfire or quit while driving. Subaru recalled these cars to replace the springs.
issues.next: Check the VIN for open recall 18V772 and have it done before driving much further. If the engine starts making a new noise or stalls, stop driving and have it towed to a dealer.

issues.t: Brake light switch can stop working
issues.sym: Brake lights that do not come on, a shifter that will not move out of Park, a push-button start that will not respond, or stability control and other warning lights on the dash.
issues.why: Fumes from some cleaning and care products used inside the car can coat the contacts in the brake light switch, so it stops sending a signal when the pedal is pressed.
issues.next: Check the VIN for recall 19V149 and have the switch replaced. Ask someone to confirm the brake lights work in the meantime, because drivers behind you may not know you are stopping.

issues.t: CVT automatic can shudder, jerk or stall
issues.sym: Shuddering or bucking at low speed, a jolt when stopped that feels like a tap from behind, the engine stalling as the car comes to a stop, or fluid spots under the front of the car.
issues.why: The first-generation continuously variable automatic had enough complaints that Subaru stretched the transmission warranty to ten years or 100,000 miles on these model years, and issued bulletins for leaks and stalling.
issues.next: The extended coverage has aged out, so have a Subaru-experienced shop check the fluid condition, look for leaks and scan for transmission codes before the problem gets worse.

issues.t: Engine computer can overheat an ignition coil and stall the engine
issues.sym: The engine suddenly loses power or stalls while driving, will not restart, or the check engine light comes on with a misfire.
issues.why: The engine computer can keep feeding power to an ignition coil after the engine is switched off. The coil overheats, can short out and blow a fuse, and the engine then shuts down.
issues.next: Check the VIN for recalls 19V743 and 21V264 and have them done promptly. If the engine stalls or misfires, have the car towed to a dealer instead of driving it.

issues.t: PCV valve can break apart and send pieces into the engine
issues.sym: Blue or white smoke from the tailpipe, oil level dropping quickly, or a sudden loss of power.
issues.why: The small crankcase ventilation valve on the engine can come apart. Pieces can be drawn into the engine, and oil gets pulled in and burned, which can end in engine damage.
issues.next: Check the VIN for recall 19V744 (or 19V856 on some 2019 cars). If you see heavy smoke or lose power, pull over, shut the engine off and have it towed.

issues.t: Rear stabilizer bar bracket bolts can work loose
issues.sym: A clunk or rattle from the rear of the car over bumps, or more body lean than usual in turns.
issues.why: The bolts holding the rear stabilizer bar brackets may not stay tight. A loose bracket can let the bar shift or come free.
issues.next: Check the VIN for recall 21V263 and have the bolts replaced and tightened. Have any new rear-end clunk looked at soon.

issues.t: Plug-in hybrid 12-volt charging connection can corrode
issues.sym: Repeated 12-volt battery warnings, a slow or dead start, or the hybrid system shutting down and leaving you without drive power.
issues.why: The terminal between the DC converter and the 12-volt battery can corrode. The corroded terminal heats up and can eventually break the connection.
issues.next: Have the VIN checked for this recall and the terminal bracket replaced. Get it done promptly, since the car can quit without warning.

issues.t: Wiring behind the dashboard can rub on a bracket and short out
issues.sym: A burning smell, blown fuses, warning lights, or electrical features cutting out.
issues.why: A wiring harness behind the instrument panel can touch a metal bracket. Over time the insulation can wear through and short, which is a fire risk.
issues.next: Check the VIN for recall 23V551 and have it inspected right away. If you smell burning or see smoke, park outside and do not drive it.

issues.t: Hybrid fuel cap seal can let fuel spill
issues.sym: A strong gasoline smell around the filler door, or fuel seeping out when the tank is close to full.
issues.why: The seal on the fuel cap of the hybrid model may not close off the filler properly, so fuel can escape. Leaking fuel near a hot or sparking part is a fire risk.
issues.next: Check the VIN for recall 26V106 and have the cap replaced. Avoid topping off the tank until then, and do not drive if you see fuel leaking.

issues.t: Water can get into the gear position switch (recall 23V-755)
issues.sym: The reverse lights and the backup camera stop working when you select reverse, and the dash may show a transmission warning.
issues.why: A weld on the inhibitor switch housing lets water inside, which corrodes the switch so it no longer reports which gear is selected.
issues.next: Have the VIN checked and the switch replaced. Until then look over your shoulder when backing up, because the camera may not come on.

issues.t: Front driveshaft can crack and break (recall 23V-754)
issues.sym: Clicking or clunking from the front when accelerating or turning, then a loss of drive even though the engine runs.
issues.why: The outer race of the front driveshaft joint can crack and come apart. If it breaks, the car may also roll when left in Park.
issues.next: Stop driving and check the VIN for this recall. The driveshaft is replaced free of charge.

issues.t: Front ball joint nut can be loose (do-not-drive recall 26V-685)
issues.sym: Clunking or knocking from the left front over bumps, or the steering feeling loose and wandering.
issues.why: The castle nut holding the left front lower ball joint may not have been tightened, so the joint can pull apart and the wheel can fold under the car.
issues.next: Do not drive the car. Subaru has issued a do-not-drive warning for this recall, so arrange a tow to the dealer for the free repair.
